conceptBreakdown.content:
Redox reactions are classified into five major groups:

1. **Combination**: $A + B \rightarrow C$ where oxidation states change (*e.g., $\text{C}(0) + \text{O}_2(0) \rightarrow \text{CO}_2(+4, -2)$*).
2. **Decomposition**: Breakdown into two or more components with at least one in elemental state (*e.g., $2\text{KClO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{KCl} + 3\text{O}_2$*).
3. **Displacement**: A metal or non-metal displaces another ion (*e.g., $\text{Zn}(s) + \text{CuSO}_4(aq) \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4(aq) + \text{Cu}(s)$*).
4. **Disproportionation**: Simultaneous oxidation and reduction of the same element.
5. **Comproportionation**: Reverse of disproportionation.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Disproportionation vs. Comproportionation
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Disproportionation vs. Comproportionation
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DISPROPORTIONATION vs COMPROPORTIONATION

Disproportionation:
• 2 H₂O₂(-1) → 2 H₂O(-2) + O₂(0)
• P₄(0) + 3 OH⁻ + 3 H₂O → PH₃(-3) + 3 H₂PO₂⁻(+1)
• Cl₂(0) + 2 OH⁻ (cold) → Cl⁻(-1) + ClO⁻(+1) + H₂O
• 3 Cl₂(0) + 6 OH⁻ (hot) → 5 Cl⁻(-1) + ClO₃⁻(+5) + 3 H₂O

Comproportionation:
• Ag(0) + Ag²⁺(aq) → 2 Ag⁺(+1)
• IO₃⁻(+5) + 5 I⁻(-1) + 6 H⁺ → 3 I₂(0) + 3 H₂O
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Disproportionation**: Occurs only when an element exists in an **intermediate oxidation state**:
  - $\text{P}_4(0) \rightarrow \text{PH}_3(-3) + \text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-(+1)$
  - $\text{Cl}_2(0) + \text{OH}^- \text{ (cold)} \rightarrow \text{Cl}^-(-1) + \text{ClO}^-(+1)$
  - $\text{Cl}_2(0) + \text{OH}^- \text{ (hot)} \rightarrow \text{Cl}^-(-1) + \text{ClO}_3^-(+5)$
  - *Fluorine Exception*: $\text{F}_2$ NEVER disproportionates because it has no positive oxidation states!

• **Comproportionation**: Two species containing the same element in different oxidation states react to form a single intermediate state (*e.g., $\text{IO}_3^-(+5) + 5\text{I}^-(-1) + 6\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 3\text{I}_2(0) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$*).

quickRevision: Disproportionation requires an intermediate oxidation state.
Fluorine (F₂) CANNOT disproportionate because it cannot exhibit positive oxidation states.
Hot alkaline Cl₂ forms Chlorate (ClO₃⁻, +5) and Chloride (Cl⁻, -1).
Comproportionation is the exact reverse of disproportionation.
